svg.text: Up to sixteen reflective IR channels on a shared pulsed LED bus, digitised on the board and read over SPI.
SPI crossing and the two converters
Pin 1 supply, Pin 2 the phototransistor emitter,
Pin 3 the LED cathode. No ground runs to the sensor.
one switch for all sixteen emitters
C3 back to V_IN at power-down
PWR-Variant B: supplied from the Teensy
to every channel, U2 and U3
Eight channels, 90 mA of the 250 mA the 3V3 pin allows.
One rail, so A1 and A2 have nothing to separate.
No fault isolation: a cable short reaches the Teensy’s regulator.
* Q2 in TO-92 has pin order 1 = G, 2 = S, 3 = D, and every figure derived from Q2 still holds the SOT-23 part’s, R42 among them.
U1 pin order: 1 = GND, 2 = IN, 3 = OUT. Most three-pin regulators run IN, GND, OUT, and wiring U1 that way puts the input on its ground pin.
C2 at U1 pin 2, C4 at U1 pin 3
shortest path for the fast current
the output capacitor is in the control loop
C5 at U2, C6 at U3, C7 at A1, C9 at A2
loop inductance to the supply pin
R33 and R41 at Q1's gate
gate loop pickup, defined gate at boot
each 4.7 kΩ at its converter input
a long stub adds capacitance to the sampling
Distances marked assumed are not datasheet figures. The MCP1700 datasheet states none.
